---
title: "Daily Share of Monthly Users by Application"
description: "The share of an application's monthly users who sign in on a typical day."
---

How often the people who use an application come back. On a typical day in the
month, what share of that month's users reached the application?

This is the standard DAU/MAU ratio, sometimes called stickiness. See [The Power
User
Curve](https://a16z.com/the-power-user-curve-the-best-way-to-understand-your-most-engaged-users/)
(Andrew Chen and Li Jin, a16z).

## Calculation

Per application and calendar month, from
[`events_app_login_counts`](../../catalog/ibm_verify_events_transformed/events_app_login_counts.qmd):

- **User-days**: the sum of daily `unique_users`.
- **Mean daily active users**: user-days divided by the days in the month. The
  table has no row for a day with no users, so dividing by the days in the month
  counts those days as zero.
- **Monthly active users**: the month's `mtd_unique_users`. It only grows within
  a month, so its maximum is the month's total even when the last day has no row.
- **Daily share of monthly users**: mean daily active users divided by monthly
  active users.
- **Active days per user**: user-days divided by monthly active users. This is the
  same ratio multiplied by the days in the month.

Only complete months are reported. A month is complete when it has ended and the
application's first row in the table falls before the 1st. Internal applications
are left out.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

```sql
WITH first_seen AS (
    SELECT application_name, MIN(CAST(from_date AS DATE)) AS first_day
    FROM ibm_verify_events_transformed.events_app_login_counts
    GROUP BY application_name
),

monthly AS (
    SELECT
        application_name,
        date_trunc('month', CAST(from_date AS DATE)) AS month,
        SUM(unique_users) AS user_days,
        -- mtd_unique_users only grows within a month, so its maximum is the
        -- month's distinct users even when the last day has no row
        MAX(mtd_unique_users) AS monthly_active_users
    FROM ibm_verify_events_transformed.events_app_login_counts
    -- set the reporting window; whole, finished calendar months only
    WHERE CAST(from_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-05-01' AND DATE '2026-09-30'
    GROUP BY 1, 2
),

services AS (
    SELECT al.alias AS application_name, s.service_name_en, s.is_internal
    FROM rp.alias al
    JOIN rp.service s ON al.rp_id = s.rp_id
),

complete AS (
    SELECT
        m.month,
        m.application_name,
        sv.service_name_en,
        day_of_month(last_day_of_month(m.month)) AS days_in_month,
        m.user_days,
        m.monthly_active_users
    FROM monthly m
    JOIN first_seen f ON m.application_name = f.application_name
    -- a left join keeps an application with no alias row
    LEFT JOIN services sv ON m.application_name = sv.application_name
    -- live for the whole month: first row before the 1st
    WHERE f.first_day < m.month
      AND NOT COALESCE(sv.is_internal, false)
)

SELECT
    month,
    application_name,
    service_name_en,
    days_in_month,
    user_days,
    CAST(user_days AS DOUBLE) / days_in_month AS mean_daily_active_users,
    monthly_active_users,
    CAST(user_days AS DOUBLE) / days_in_month / monthly_active_users
        AS dau_mau_ratio,
    CAST(user_days AS DOUBLE) / monthly_active_users AS active_days_per_user
FROM complete
ORDER BY month, dau_mau_ratio DESC;
```

## R

```r
app_logins <- tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_transformed", "events_app_login_counts"))

first_seen <- app_logins |>
  group_by(application_name) |>
  summarise(first_day = min(as.Date(from_date), na.rm = TRUE))

services <- tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "alias")) |>
  inner_join(tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "service")), by = "rp_id") |>
  select(application_name = alias, service_name_en, is_internal)

app_logins |>
  # set the reporting window; whole, finished calendar months only
  filter(
    as.Date(from_date) >= as.Date("2026-05-01"),
    as.Date(from_date) <= as.Date("2026-09-30")
  ) |>
  group_by(application_name, month = floor_date(as.Date(from_date), "month")) |>
  summarise(
    user_days = sum(unique_users, na.rm = TRUE),
    # mtd_unique_users only grows within a month, so its maximum is the
    # month's distinct users even when the last day has no row
    monthly_active_users = max(mtd_unique_users, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  inner_join(first_seen, by = "application_name") |>
  # live for the whole month: first row before the 1st
  filter(first_day < month) |>
  # a left join keeps an application with no alias row
  left_join(services, by = "application_name") |>
  filter(!coalesce(is_internal, FALSE)) |>
  mutate(
    days_in_month = day(last_day_of_month(month)),
    mean_daily_active_users = as.double(user_days) / days_in_month,
    dau_mau_ratio = as.double(user_days) / days_in_month / monthly_active_users,
    active_days_per_user = as.double(user_days) / monthly_active_users
  ) |>
  select(
    month, application_name, service_name_en, days_in_month, user_days,
    mean_daily_active_users, monthly_active_users, dau_mau_ratio,
    active_days_per_user
  ) |>
  arrange(month, desc(dau_mau_ratio))
```

:::

:::

## Interpretation notes

The lowest possible value is one divided by the days in the month, about 3%. It
means every user came on exactly one day. The highest is 100%, meaning every user
came every day. Active days per user is often easier to read: 2.5 means a typical
monthly user signed in on two or three days.

**Partial months are left out.** A month-to-date figure is biased high, not just
noisy. On the 1st, everyone active that day is the whole month's base, so the
ratio is 100%. It then falls as occasional users join the base. A trailing 28-day
window avoids this, but it needs per-user data that the summary tables do not
hold.

**Read a service with several applications row by row.** Each row is exact for
its application. Adding rows together counts someone who used both applications
twice, in both the numerator and the denominator, by an amount that cannot be
recovered.

**`unique_users` counts users with any SSO event, successful or not.** Failed
events almost always carry the user ID `"UNKNOWN"`, which counts as one user. It
only matters for applications with a handful of users.

**This is an average.** It does not show whether most users come once or a few
come daily. The per-user version, a histogram of users by days active in the
month (the "L30"), needs per-user data.

## Alternative names

- DAU/MAU ratio
- stickiness
- engagement ratio
- sign-in frequency by application
- active days per user
